related_questions.question: Can chorea go away?
related_questions.snippet: Chorea in people who have hyperthyroidism or hyperglycemia usually lessens when that disorder is treated. Sydenham chorea and chorea caused by a stroke often gradually subside without treatment. If chorea is caused by a medication or other substance, stopping it may help, but the chorea does not always disappear.

text_blocks.snippet: Treatment for movement disorders is multifaceted and tailored to the specific condition and individual needs. It often involves a combination of medications, therapies, and in some cases, surgical interventions.
snippet_highlighted_words: It often involves a combination of medications, therapies, and in some cases, surgical interventions

list.title: To manage muscle symptoms:
list.snippet: Muscle relaxants, medications targeting specific neurotransmitters, and drugs like levodopa for Parkinson's disease are used.

list.title: To reduce tremors:
list.snippet: Beta blockers, anti-seizure medications, and anticholinergic agents are employed.

list.title: To address dystonia:
list.snippet: Anticholinergic agents, anti-anxiety medications, and botulinum toxin injections can help manage muscle spasms and stiffness.

list.title: For other conditions:
list.snippet: Medications like antipsychotics (e.g., haloperidol) are used for Tourette's syndrome.
Physical therapy: Improves mobility, reduces stiffness, and manages pain.
Occupational therapy: Enhances functional skills and daily living activities.
Speech therapy: Addresses speech and swallowing difficulties.
Rehabilitation: May include physical, occupational, and speech therapy to improve movement, coordination, and overall function.
Deep brain stimulation (DBS): An implantable device delivers electrical stimulation to targeted brain areas to regulate movement.
Ablation surgery: Involves lesioning specific brain areas to disrupt abnormal neural activity.
Medication pumps: May be used to deliver medications directly to the brain or spinal cord.

list.title: Botulinum toxin injections:
list.snippet: Used to relax muscles and reduce spasms, especially in focal dystonia, tics, and certain aspects of Parkinson's.

list.title: Clinical trials:
list.snippet: Offer access to cutting-edge treatments and research.

list.title: Supportive therapies:
list.snippet: May include nutrition counseling, mental health support, and community resources.

list.title: Complementary therapies:
list.snippet: Some individuals find yoga, meditation, and other practices helpful in managing symptoms.
